def-glh-reduced-model.title: Reduced model and linear hypothesis
def-glh-reduced-model.html: Let X0 be an n×p0 matrix with C(X0)⊆C(X) and r0=rank(X0)<r. The reduced model is E(Y)=X0c, c∈Rp0. Inside the full model it corresponds to the linear hypothesis 𝛃𝛃𝛃H0: Xβ∈C(X0)againstH1: Xβ∈C(X), Xβ∉C(X0). The number q=r−r0 is the number of degrees of freedom of the hypothesis, and we write M and M0 for the orthogonal projections onto C(X) and C(X0).

def-glh-testable.title: Testable hypothesis
def-glh-testable.html:
Let Λ be a p×m matrix and d∈Rm. The hypothesis 𝛃H:Λ⊤β=d is testable if

  1. 𝛃Λ⊤β is estimable, that is, C(Λ)⊆C(X⊤) (@def-est-estimable and @thm-est-characterization), so that Λ=X⊤T for some n×m matrix T; and

  2. the equations Λ⊤b=d are consistent, that is, d∈C(Λ⊤) (@thm-mat-consistency).

Its number of degrees of freedom is q=rank(Λ). We assume q≥1.

eq-glh-F.html: F=(SSE0−SSE)/(r−r0)SSE/(n−r)=y⊤(M−M0)y/qy⊤(I−M)y/(n−r)

eq-glh-general-F.html: 𝛃𝛃SSH=(Λ⊤β^−d)⊤W−(Λ⊤β^−d),FH=SSH/qSSE/(n−r).

eq-glh-general-noncentrality.html: 𝛃𝛃γ=(Λ⊤β−d)⊤W−(Λ⊤β−d)σ2,

eq-glh-lr.html: Λ=(SSESSEH)n/2=(1+qFHn−r)−n/2,

eq-glh-noncentrality.html: 𝛃F∼F(r−r0, n−r, γ),γ=‖(M−M0)Xβ‖2σ2;

eq-glh-power.html: π(γ)=Pr{F(q,n−r,γ)>Fα(q,n−r)},

eq-glh-t.html: 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌T=λ⊤β^−dsλ⊤Gλ,s2=SSEn−r.

eq-glh-three-spaces.html: Rn=C(X0)⏟dim⁡r0⊕C(X)∩C(X0)⊥⏟dim⁡q=r−r0⊕C(X)⊥⏟dim⁡n−r,I=M0+(M−M0)+(I−M).

exm-glh-group-size.title: How many observations per group?
exm-glh-group-size.html:
Four treatments are to be compared at level 0.05, and a spread of one standard deviation between the best and the worst treatment (Δ/σ=1) should be detected with probability at least 0.9. The noncentrality per observation per group is 0.500 for the least favourable configuration, 0.556 for equally spaced means, and 1.000 for the most favourable one (two means at each end). Searching over m with @eq-glh-power gives

Configuration γ/m smallest m with power ≥0.9 power at that m
least favourable 0.500 30 0.907
equally spaced 0.556 27 0.906
most favourable 1.000 16 0.917

To be safe against every configuration with range at least σ, the study needs 30 observations per group. A simulation of 20000 data sets at the least favourable configuration with m=30 rejects in a proportion 0.909 of them, against the computed 0.907. Figure 11.5.1 shows the whole power curves.

exm-glh-longley.title: Jointly significant, individually not
exm-glh-longley.html:
Longley’s data record US employment for the 16 years 1947 to 1962, with five economic series: the GNP deflator, GNP, unemployment, the size of the armed forces and population. Regress employment on the five series and an intercept, leaving out the time trend, so that n−p=10. For unemployment and population, the t statistics are −0.921 and −1.222, with p-values 0.379 and 0.250. Neither comes near the critical value 2.228. The test that both coefficients are zero gives F=7.175 on 2 and 10 degrees of freedom, p=0.0117.

Figure 11.6.1 shows why. The two estimates have correlation −0.840. Under the hypothesis, their t statistics are then likely to have opposite signs, and the F test’s acceptance region is an ellipse stretched along the line t1=−t2. The observed pair has both statistics negative, a combination the ellipse excludes although each coordinate on its own is unremarkable. The data are clear that unemployment and population together matter, and unclear about how to divide the credit. With 16 consecutive years of trending series, the errors are also unlikely to be independent, a caution taken up in Chapter 21.

exm-glh-region.title: Do regions matter?
exm-glh-region.html:
In the 2009 data on 50 US states used in Chapter 6 and Chapter 9, regress the murder rate on the poverty rate, the percentage of single-parent households and the percentage living in urbanized areas, with an intercept. This is the reduced model, with r0=4. The full model adds indicators of three of the four Census regions (Northeast, South, West, with the Midwest as reference), so r=7. The question is whether the regions differ in murder rate once the three covariates are accounted for. The listing gives

Source Degrees of freedom Sum of squares Mean square
Regions, given the covariates 3 14.83 4.944
Residual, full model 43 87.13 2.026
Residual, reduced model 46 101.96

so F=4.944/2.026=2.440 on 3 and 43 degrees of freedom. The 5% critical value is 2.822 and the p-value is 0.077. At the conventional level the reduced model is not rejected. The data do not show convincingly that the regions differ, given the covariates.

Yet in the full model the Northeast coefficient is −1.736 murders per 100,000, with a t statistic of −2.519 and a p-value of 0.016. One of the three contrasts looks clearly nonzero while the joint test does not reject. There is no contradiction: Section 11.6 shows how a joint test can dilute one strong effect among weak ones, and Chapter 13 explains why a contrast singled out after looking at the estimates cannot be judged by its own p-value.

exm-glh-region-angle.title: The region test as an angle
exm-glh-region-angle.title_html: The region test as an angle
exm-glh-region-angle.html:
In @exm-glh-region, the reduced model’s residual vector has a component of length 3.851 in the three-dimensional test space and a component of length 9.334 in the 43-dimensional residual space. The angle between the residual vector and the test space is θ=67.6∘, and the partial R2 is cos2⁡θ=0.145. The 5% test rejects when θ<66.1∘, so the data fall just outside the cone.

Figure 11.2.1 plots the two lengths for the data and for 4000 simulated data sets. With the reduced model true, 0.053 of them fall in the rejection region. With the Northeast lowered by two murders per 100,000, and all else as fitted, the fraction is 0.774.

exm-glh-regions-rank-deficient.title: Regional hypotheses with an over-parameterized model
exm-glh-regions-rank-deficient.title_html: Regional hypotheses with an over-parameterized model
exm-glh-regions-rank-deficient.html:
Return to the state murder data, now with an intercept and an indicator for each of the four regions, so that 𝛃β=(μ,αN,αM,αS,αW,βpov,βsin,βurb)⊤. The model matrix is 50×8 of rank 7. No region effect is estimable on its own, but every contrast among them is.

All four regions equal. Write the hypothesis with all six pairwise differences αi−αj as the columns of Λ. They are consistent and have rank q=3. With the Moore–Penrose inverses of X⊤X and of W, @eq-glh-general-F gives SSH=14.83 and F=2.440, exactly the reduced-model test of @exm-glh-region, as @thm-glh-general-f(b) requires. A second generalized inverse, made by deleting the row and column of αW from X⊤X before inverting, gives a different 𝛃β^ but the same 𝛃Λ⊤β^, W and F.

Midwest, South and West equal. With Λ made of αM−αS and αS−αW, the sum of squares is 3.881 on 2 degrees of freedom, F=0.958, p=0.392. The restricted fit of @prp-glh-restricted-ls coincides with the fit of the model in which the three regions are merged. Under the constraint, the Northeast lies 1.379 below the common level of the other three, and the coefficient of single parenthood moves from 0.428 to 0.441.

A nonzero right-hand side. The contrast αN−(αM+αS+αW)/3, the Northeast against the average of the other regions, is estimated as ψ^=−1.426 with standard error 0.595. To test whether it equals −1, take the offset b0=(0,−1,0,…,0)⊤ and fit y−Xb0 on a basis of S0. The drop in residual sum of squares is 1.040, equal to 𝛌𝛌(ψ^+1)2/λ⊤Gλ as @eq-glh-general-F predicts, and F=0.513 with p=0.478. Any other solution of 𝛌λ⊤b0=−1 gives the same answer.

A constraint that is not a hypothesis. The constraint αN=0 is not estimable. Minimizing the residual sum of squares subject to it gives exactly SSE: the constrained model spans the whole of C(X), in agreement with @prp-glh-nonestimable.

exm-glh-spherical.title: Four error laws
exm-glh-spherical.html:
Keep the design of @exm-glh-region and simulate 20000 data sets with the reduced model true, each with errors from one of four laws: independent normal; spherical t with three degrees of freedom; independent t with three degrees of freedom; independent centred exponential. The spherical errors are uncorrelated, but their sizes move together: the rank correlation between the absolute values of two components is 0.20. The rejection rates of the 5% test are

Errors normal spherical t3 independent t3 exponential
Rejection rate 0.0502 0.0502 0.0444 0.0474

with Monte Carlo standard error about 0.0015. The first two agree exactly, not just approximately: the spherical errors were made by rescaling the normal ones, and each rescaled data set gives the same F as its normal original. The two independent non-normal laws give rates slightly below 0.05. For this design, with 43 residual degrees of freedom and no extreme leverage, the independent t3 errors make the test slightly conservative, the exponential rate is within Monte Carlo error of 0.05, and both are close to the nominal level.

exm-glh-state-coefficients.title: Five regressors for the murder rate
exm-glh-state-coefficients.title_html: Five regressors for the murder rate
exm-glh-state-coefficients.html:
Regress the murder rate of the 50 states on poverty, high-school graduation, single-parent households, percentage white and urbanization, with an intercept (p=6, n−p=44).

Regressor Estimate Standard error t p-value
intercept −10.0586 17.6785 −0.569 0.572
poverty 0.2378 0.1412 1.684 0.099
high-school graduates −0.0047 0.1530 −0.030 0.976
single-parent households 0.4280 0.1372 3.120 0.003
white 0.0108 0.0270 0.398 0.692
urban 0.0046 0.0145 0.315 0.754

The overall test gives R2=0.643 and F=15.87 on 5 and 44 degrees of freedom, p=6.4×10−9. Only single parenthood has a t statistic beyond the critical value 2.015. The group of three demographic and educational regressors, high-school graduation, percentage white and urbanization, has F=0.096 on 3 and 44 degrees of freedom, p=0.962: the data give no evidence that these three add anything once poverty and single parenthood are in the model. Every tj2 of the group is at most 3F=0.29, as @prp-glh-max-t requires.

This group was chosen here because its members have small t statistics. A group selected that way will tend to have a small F, and its large p-value makes dropping the group look safer than it is. Groups should be defined by the scientific question, before the individual results are seen.

exm-glh-trinity.title: Three verdicts from one data set
exm-glh-trinity.title_html: Three verdicts from one data set
exm-glh-trinity.html:
For the region test of @exm-glh-region, n=50, q=3 and n−r=43. The three statistics are

Statistic Value p-value from χ2(3)
Wald 8.512 0.0365
Likelihood ratio, −2log⁡Λ 7.861 0.0490
Score 7.274 0.0637
F=2.440, exact 0.0773

With the 5% critical value 7.815 of χ2(3), the Wald test rejects, the likelihood ratio test rejects barely, and the score test does not. The exact test, which all three approximate, does not reject. The disagreement is not a paradox. The approximate tests are different tests, and their true sizes differ from 0.05. With q=3 and r=7, the formulas of @prp-glh-trinity give

n 15 30 50 100 400
Wald 0.315 0.143 0.097 0.071 0.055
Likelihood ratio 0.221 0.106 0.079 0.063 0.053
Score 0.102 0.069 0.060 0.055 0.051

At the sample size of the example the nominal 5% Wald test has true size close to 10%. All three sizes approach 0.05 as n grows, but slowly when r is not small compared with n.

exr-glh-angle-numbers.title: A1
exr-glh-angle-numbers.html: Use @prp-glh-angle to express cos2⁡θ in terms of F, q and n−r. Check the value 0.145 of @exm-glh-region-angle from F=2.440, q=3 and n−r=43, and compute θα from F0.05(3,43)=2.822.

exr-glh-beta-null.title: B1
exr-glh-beta-null.html: Show that under H0 the squared cosine cos2⁡θ of @prp-glh-angle has the Beta(q/2,(n−r)/2) distribution, and that it is independent of ‖(I−M0)Y‖2. What is its expectation?

exr-glh-chain.title: B3
exr-glh-chain.html: Let C(X0)⊆C(X1)⊆C(X) with ranks r0<r1<r<n, and let s2=SSE/(n−r) come from the largest model. Show that F1=y⊤(M1−M0)y/(r1−r0)s2 has the F(r1−r0,n−r,γ1) distribution with 𝛃γ1=‖(M1−M0)Xβ‖2/σ2 whenever the largest model holds, and that its numerator is independent of that of the test of X1 within X. Why is this preferable to using the residual mean square of X1?

exr-glh-chow.title: B4
exr-glh-chow.html: Two samples of sizes n1 and n2 follow 𝛃E(Yk)=Xkβk, k=1,2, with a common σ2 and Xk of full column rank p. Write the model for both samples together as a full model with block-diagonal model matrix, and the hypothesis 𝛃𝛃β1=β2 as a reduced model. Show that F=(SSEpooled−SSE1−SSE2)/p(SSE1+SSE2)/(n1+n2−2p), where SSEk comes from fitting sample k alone and SSEpooled from one fit to all the data. Apply the test to the question whether two firms of the Grunfeld panel (sm.datasets.grunfeld) share their investment equation, and comment on the assumption of a common σ2.

exr-glh-chow-few.title: C1
exr-glh-chow-few.html: In @exr-glh-chow suppose instead that n2≤p and rank(X2)=n2, so that 𝛃β2 cannot be estimated from the second sample. Show that the full model then fits the second sample exactly, identify the test space, and show that the F statistic of @thm-glh-f-test becomes F=(SSEpooled−SSE1)/n2SSE1/(n1−p), a test of whether the second sample is predicted by the fit to the first, on n2 and n1−p degrees of freedom.

exr-glh-critical-growth.title: B2
exr-glh-critical-growth.html: Show that qFα(q,ν) is strictly increasing in q for fixed ν and α. Deduce that a single t statistic with t2 just above Fα(1,ν) does not force the rejection of a group containing it.

exr-glh-eliminate.title: C2
exr-glh-eliminate.html: Let X have full column rank and write Λ⊤=[Λ1⊤,Λ2⊤] with Λ2⊤ a nonsingular q×q block, after permuting the coefficients so that 𝛃𝛃𝛃β=(β1⊤,β2⊤)⊤ conformably. Show that 𝛃Λ⊤β=0 is equivalent to 𝛃𝛃β2=−Λ2−⊤Λ1⊤β1, that the reduced model matrix is X1−X2Λ2−⊤Λ1⊤, and that this matrix has full column rank p−q. This is how the reduced model is fitted when no offset or null-space basis is at hand.

exr-glh-equal-coefficients.title: B1
exr-glh-equal-coefficients.html: In a full-rank model, show that the t statistic for βj=βk is T=β^j−β^kscjj+ckk−2cjk, where cjk are the entries of (X⊤X)−1. Show that it equals the t statistic of the coefficient of xj in the reparameterized model with regressors xj and xj+xk in place of xj and xk.

exr-glh-invariance-shift.title: A1
exr-glh-invariance-shift.html: Show that the F statistic @eq-glh-F does not change when y is replaced by ay+X0c for any a≠0 and any vector c. Interpret the result for the region test of @exm-glh-region when murder rates are expressed per million instead of per 100,000.

exr-glh-k2.title: C1
exr-glh-k2.html: In the sensitivity calculation, let nN be the number of Northeast states and RN2 the coefficient of determination from regressing the Northeast indicator on the reduced model’s columns (which include 1). Show that ‖(I−M0)dN‖2=nN(1−nN/n)(1−RN2). Interpret each factor, and relate the formula to @eq-proj-vif-preview.

exr-glh-known-sigma.title: B1
exr-glh-known-sigma.html: Suppose σ2=σ02 is known. Show that X2=(SSE0−SSE)/σ02 has the χ2(q,γ) distribution and that the test rejecting when X2 exceeds the upper α point of χ2(q) has level α. Show that qF/X2→1 in probability as n→∞ with q fixed and the full model true, and explain why the F test and this test then behave alike.

exr-glh-known-sigma-lr.title: B3
exr-glh-known-sigma-lr.html: Suppose σ2=σ02 is known. Show that the likelihood ratio test of a reduced model rejects for large (SSE0−SSE)/σ02, the statistic of @exr-glh-known-sigma, and that −2log⁡Λ is then exactly χ2(q) under H0.

exr-glh-longley-F.title: B3
exr-glh-longley-F.html: For two coefficients with t statistics t1,t2 whose estimates have correlation ρ, show that the F statistic for both being zero is F=t12+t22−2ρt1t22(1−ρ2). Check the value 7.175 of @exm-glh-longley from t1=−0.921, t2=−1.222 and ρ=−0.840, and find the value of F had the correlation been +0.840.

exr-glh-lr-numbers.title: A1
exr-glh-lr-numbers.html: From F=2.440, q=3, n=50 and r=7, compute the three statistics of @prp-glh-trinity and check them against @exm-glh-trinity.

exr-glh-maximal-invariant.title: C1
exr-glh-maximal-invariant.html: In the canonical form, let two data vectors y and y′ with z2,z2′≠0 have the same value of F. Construct a>0, v∈C(X0) and an orthogonal H of the kind allowed in @prp-glh-invariance such that y′=aHy+v. (So F is a maximal invariant: any statistic unchanged by these transformations is a function of F.)

exr-glh-mean-specified.title: B4
exr-glh-mean-specified.html: Show that the hypothesis 𝛃𝛃Xβ=Xβ0, with 𝛃β0 known, is testable, that q=r, and that its F statistic is 𝛃{‖M(y−Xβ0)‖2/r}/s2. What is the reduced model?

exr-glh-mlr-general.title: C2
exr-glh-mlr-general.html: Extend @lem-glh-mlr: show that for 0≤γ1<γ2 the ratio fγ2(x)/fγ1(x) is increasing in x. (Write both densities as power series in t(x) with coefficients ak(γ), and show that ak(γ2)/ak(γ1) increases with k.) Deduce that the F test is also uniformly most powerful invariant for testing γ≤γ1 against γ>γ1, with a noncentral critical value. Such tests appear in equivalence testing.

exr-glh-no-ump.title: C1
exr-glh-no-ump.html: In the canonical form with σ2 known and q≥2, consider testing 𝛈η1=0 against the single alternative 𝛈η1=a≠0. Show by the Neyman–Pearson lemma that the most powerful level-α test rejects when a⊤z1>σ‖a‖zα, where zα is the upper α point of N(0,1). Show that this test has power below α against −a, and conclude that no uniformly most powerful test of 𝛈η1=0 exists.

exr-glh-non-spherical-size.title: C2
exr-glh-non-spherical-size.html: Take a one-way layout with two groups of sizes n1=5 and n2=20, independent normal errors with standard deviations 3 in the small group and 1 in the large one, and equal means. Compute, by simulation or numerical integration, the true level of the nominal 5% F test of equal means. Explain the direction of the error using the angle picture: which way does the unequal variance tilt the residual vector?

exr-glh-nonestimable-formula.title: C1
exr-glh-nonestimable-formula.html: In the one-way layout with two groups of sizes 2 and 3, take Λ=(0,1,0)⊤, so that the “hypothesis” is α1=0. Evaluate 𝛃(Λ⊤β^)2/(Λ⊤GΛ) for two different generalized inverses G of X⊤X and show that the values differ. Explain which step of the proof of @thm-glh-general-f fails.

exr-glh-nr2.title: B2
exr-glh-nr2.html: Let 𝛆𝛃ε^H=y−Xβ^H be the residual vector of the restricted fit. Show that the score statistic equals 𝛆𝛆n‖Mε^H‖2/‖ε^H‖2, which is n times the uncentred R2 from regressing 𝛆ε^H on X. Explain why this “nR2” recipe needs only the restricted fit.

exr-glh-observed-half.title: B3
exr-glh-observed-half.html: For q=1 and large n−r, the F test is approximately the test that rejects when |Z|>zα/2, with Z∼N(δ,1). Show that if the observed |z| equals zα/2 exactly, the observed power Pr{|Z|>zα/2} at δ=zα/2 is just above 1/2. Conclude that a result on the edge of significance always has observed power about one half, whatever the design.

exr-glh-one-sided-choice.title: A2
exr-glh-one-sided-choice.html: Show that if the direction of a one-sided t test is chosen after seeing the sign of T, and the test then rejects when |T|>tn−r,α, its size is 2α.

exr-glh-one-sided-lrt.title: C2
exr-glh-one-sided-lrt.html: Find the likelihood ratio test of 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β≤d against 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β>d for estimable 𝛌λ, and show that it rejects for large values of T in @eq-glh-t. (Maximize the likelihood under the inequality constraint: if 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^≤d the unrestricted maximum is feasible; otherwise the maximum is on the boundary.)

exr-glh-poverty-t.title: A1
exr-glh-poverty-t.html: Using the table of @exm-glh-state-coefficients, compute the F statistic for dropping poverty from the five-regressor model and its p-value, without refitting.

exr-glh-reduced-examples.title: A2
exr-glh-reduced-examples.html: In the model E(Yi)=β0+β1xi1+β2xi2+β3xi3, write down a matrix X0 (or an offset and an X0) for each reduced model and give q: (i) β2=β3=0; (ii) β1=β2=β3; (iii) β1=2; (iv) β2+β3=0.

exr-glh-reformulate.title: B1
exr-glh-reformulate.html: Let Λ be p×m and A a nonsingular m×m matrix. Show that the hypotheses 𝛃Λ⊤β=d and 𝛃(ΛA)⊤β=A⊤d are the same, and that @eq-glh-general-F gives the same SSH for both. Conclude that the test does not depend on how a set of constraints is written.

exr-glh-replication.title: B2
exr-glh-replication.html: Take the straight-line model with design points 0,1,2,3, one observation each, and the hypothesis β1=0. Compute γ as a multiple of β12/σ2 and the power at β1/σ=1, level 0.05. Then compare (i) replicating the design twice, (ii) adding four observations at x=3, and (iii) adding four observations at x=1.5. Verify @thm-glh-power(c) in each case and explain the ranking.

exr-glh-restricted-moments.title: B2
exr-glh-restricted-moments.html: In @prp-glh-restricted-ls, show that 𝛃𝛃𝛃E(Xβ^H)=Xβ−MTW−1(Λ⊤β−d) and 𝛃Cov(Xβ^H)=σ2PS0, where PS0=M−MTW−1T⊤M. Conclude that restricted fitted values are unbiased when H holds, have smaller variance than MY in every direction, and are biased when H fails.

exr-glh-scheffe-preview.title: C1
exr-glh-scheffe-preview.html: Show that 𝛌maxT(λ)2 over all nonzero estimable 𝛌λ, for the hypotheses 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β=0, equals rF∗, where F∗ is the statistic for the reduced model E(Y)=0. Deduce that 𝛌𝛌Pr{T(λ)2≤rFα(r,n−r) for all estimable λ}=1−α when 𝛃β=0. What changes if 𝛃β≠0 and 𝛌T(λ) is centred at 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β? (Chapter 13 builds simultaneous inference on this.)

exr-glh-slope-one.title: B3
exr-glh-slope-one.html: In simple regression E(Yi)=β0+β1xi, derive the F statistic for β1=1 in two ways: from @eq-glh-general-F, and by regressing yi−xi on an intercept and comparing with the full fit. Show that both give F=(β^1−1)2Sxx/s2.

exr-glh-slope-power.title: A1
exr-glh-slope-power.html: For the test of β1=0 in simple regression, show that γ=β12Sxx/σ2, with Sxx=∑i(xi−x¯)2. With n=20 design points in [0,1], compare Sxx for equal spacing and for ten points at each end. What does the second design give up?

exr-glh-small-F.title: B2
exr-glh-small-F.html: Suppose the full model is wrong: 𝛍E(Y)=μ with 𝛍𝛅(I−M)μ=δ≠0, but 𝛍(M−M0)μ=0. Show that the numerator and denominator of @eq-glh-F are still independent, that E(numerator)=σ2 and 𝛅E(denominator)=σ2+‖δ‖2/(n−r), and that Pr(F≤c)≥Pr{F(q,n−r)≤c} for every c>0. Explain why an F statistic far below one, with a p-value near one, is a hint that the full model is inadequate.

exr-glh-spherical-examples.title: B3
exr-glh-spherical-examples.html: Which of the following error vectors satisfy the hypothesis of @prp-glh-spherical? (i) 𝛆ε=σZ with σ fixed; (ii) 𝛆ε=SZ with S uniform on (1,2) and independent of Z; (iii) 𝛆ε with independent Laplace components; (iv) 𝛆ε=DZ with D a fixed diagonal matrix with unequal entries; (v) 𝛆ε=Z/‖Z‖2.

exr-glh-test-space.title: B2
exr-glh-test-space.html: Prove that C(M−M0)=C((I−M0)X), and that for X=[X0,X2] this equals C((I−M0)X2). Show that dim⁡C((I−M0)X2)=rank(X)−rank(X0).

exr-glh-testable-oneway.title: A1
exr-glh-testable-oneway.html: In the one-way layout E(Yij)=μ+αi, i=1,2,3, with all groups nonempty, decide which of the following are testable hypotheses: (i) α1=α2; (ii) α1=0; (iii) α1+α2+α3=0; (iv) μ+α1=5; (v) α1−α2=1, α2−α3=2, α1−α3=3; (vi) α1−α2=1, α2−α3=2, α1−α3=4. Give q for those that are.

exr-glh-unbalanced-gamma.title: A2
exr-glh-unbalanced-gamma.html: For the one-way layout with group sizes n1,…,ng, show that the noncentrality of the test of equal means is γ=∑ini(μi−μ¯w)2/σ2, with μ¯w=∑iniμi/n.

exr-glh-unbalanced-lf.title: B1
exr-glh-unbalanced-lf.html: Extend @prp-glh-least-favourable to unequal group sizes: show that among configurations with range Δ, γ ≥ Δ2σ211/n(1)+1/n(2), where n(1)≤n(2) are the two smallest group sizes, and describe the configuration attaining it.

exr-glh-wilks.title: B1
exr-glh-wilks.html: Fix q and r. Show that under H, as n→∞, qFH converges in distribution to χ2(q), and that the differences Wald−qFH, −2log⁡Λ−qFH and Score−qFH converge to zero in probability. Deduce that the sizes in @exm-glh-trinity tend to 0.05.

lem-glh-mlr.title: Monotone likelihood ratio of the noncentral F
lem-glh-mlr.title_html: Monotone likelihood ratio of the noncentral F
lem-glh-mlr.html: For q,ν≥1 let fγ be the density of F(q,ν,γ). For every γ>0, the ratio fγ(x)/f0(x) is a strictly increasing function of x>0.

prp-glh-angle.title: F as a function of an angle
prp-glh-angle.title_html: F as a function of an angle
prp-glh-angle.html: Let w=(I−M0)y≠0 and let θ∈[0,π/2] be the angle between w and the test space, defined by cos⁡θ=‖(M−M0)y‖/‖w‖. Then ‖(M−M0)y‖2=‖w‖2cos2⁡θ,SSE=‖w‖2sin2⁡θ,F=n−rqcot2⁡θ. The partial coefficient of determination of @def-ss-partial-r2 is cos2⁡θ, and the F test rejects exactly when θ<θα, where tan2⁡θα=(n−r)/{qFα(q,n−r)}.

prp-glh-canonical.title: Canonical form of a linear hypothesis
prp-glh-canonical.title_html: Canonical form of a linear hypothesis
prp-glh-canonical.html:
Let Q=[Q0,Q1,Q2] be an orthogonal n×n matrix whose blocks of r0, q and n−r columns are orthonormal bases of C(X0), of the test space and of C(X)⊥. Put zk=Qk⊤Y and 𝛈𝛃ηk=Qk⊤Xβ, k=0,1,2. Under @eq-opt-normal-model:

  1. z0,z1,z2 are independent, 𝛈zk∼N(ηk,σ2I), and 𝛈η2=0;

  2. ‖z1‖2=SSE0−SSE and ‖z2‖2=SSE, so F={‖z1‖2/q}/{‖z2‖2/(n−r)};

  3. 𝛈‖η1‖2=σ2γ, and H0 holds iff 𝛈η1=0.

prp-glh-invariance.title: Invariance of the F statistic
prp-glh-invariance.title_html: Invariance of the F statistic
prp-glh-invariance.html: The statistic @eq-glh-F depends on X and X0 only through C(X) and C(X0). Where it is defined, that is, when (I−M)y≠0, it is unchanged when y is replaced by aHy+v,a≠0,v∈C(X0), where H is any orthogonal matrix that maps C(X0) onto itself and C(X) onto itself.

prp-glh-least-favourable.title: Least and most favourable configurations
prp-glh-least-favourable.html: In the balanced one-way layout with g≥2 groups of m observations, group means μ1,…,μg and common variance σ2, the noncentrality of the F test of equal means is γ=mσ2∑i=1g(μi−μ¯)2,μ¯=1g∑iμi. Among configurations whose range maxiμi−miniμi equals Δ, mΔ22σ2 ≤ γ ≤ mgΔ24σ2. The lower bound is attained exactly when one mean is at each extreme and all others are at the midpoint. For even g, the upper bound is attained exactly when half the means are at each extreme.

prp-glh-max-t.title: The group statistic is the largest single statistic
prp-glh-max-t.title_html: The group statistic is the largest single statistic
prp-glh-max-t.html: Let 𝛃H:Λ⊤β=d be testable with Λ of full column rank q, let FH be its statistic @eq-glh-general-F, and for a∈Rq, a≠0, let T(a) be the t statistic @eq-glh-t for the single function 𝛃a⊤Λ⊤β=a⊤d. Then qFH=maxa≠0T(a)2, and the maximum is attained at 𝛃a∝W−1(Λ⊤β^−d), where W=Λ⊤GΛ. In particular tj2≤qFH for each coefficient βj in a tested group βj=0, j∈J, with q=|J|.

prp-glh-nonestimable.title: Nonestimable constraints cannot be tested
prp-glh-nonestimable.html:
Let 𝛌λ∉C(X⊤) and c∈R.

  1. For every 𝛃β∈Rp there is 𝛃β′ with 𝛃𝛃Xβ′=Xβ and 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β′=c.

  2. Let ϕ be any test of 𝛌𝛃H:λ⊤β=c in the model @eq-opt-normal-model, with rejection probability 𝛃𝛃π(β,σ2)=Eβ,σ2ϕ(Y). For every point 𝛃(β,σ2) of the alternative there is a point 𝛃(β′,σ2) of the hypothesis with 𝛃𝛃π(β′,σ2)=π(β,σ2). So no test has power exceeding its size anywhere.

prp-glh-observed-power.title: Observed power is a function of the p-value
prp-glh-observed-power.title_html: Observed power is a function of the p-value
prp-glh-observed-power.html: Fix q, n−r and α, and define the observed power as π(γ^), with π as in @eq-glh-power and γ^=qFobs. Then the observed power is a strictly decreasing function of the p-value of the F test. The same holds for any estimate γ^=h(Fobs) with h strictly increasing and positive.

prp-glh-p-value.title: The p-value is uniform under the hypothesis
prp-glh-p-value.title_html: The p-value is uniform under the hypothesis
prp-glh-p-value.html: Under H0, the p-value p(Y) has the uniform distribution on (0,1). For every α∈(0,1), rejecting when p(Y)≤α is the F test at level α.

prp-glh-restricted-ls.title: Least squares under a testable hypothesis
prp-glh-restricted-ls.title_html: Least squares under a testable hypothesis
prp-glh-restricted-ls.html:
Let 𝛃H:Λ⊤β=d be testable with Λ of full column rank q, and write Λ=X⊤T. Let G be a generalized inverse of X⊤X, 𝛃β^=GX⊤y, W=Λ⊤GΛ and 𝛃u=Λ⊤β^−d. Then W is positive definite, and:

  1. 𝛃𝛃β^H=β^−GΛW−1u satisfies 𝛃Λ⊤β^H=d and minimizes ‖y−Xb‖2 subject to Λ⊤b=d. The set of all minimizers is 𝛃β^H+(N(X)∩N(Λ⊤)).

  2. The restricted fitted vector is unique: 𝛃Xβ^H=My−MTW−1u=Xb0+PS0(y−Xb0), and 𝛃‖y−Xβ^H‖2=SSE+SSH, with SSH=u⊤W−1u.

  3. With 𝛉θ^=W−1u, the restricted estimate solves the constrained normal equations (compare @thm-proj-normal-equations) 𝛃𝛉𝛃X⊤Xβ^H+Λθ^=X⊤y,Λ⊤β^H=d,

    and 𝛉𝛉SSH=θ^⊤Wθ^.

prp-glh-spherical.title: Spherical errors
prp-glh-spherical.html: Let 𝛃𝛆Y=Xβ+ε with 𝛃Xβ∈C(X0), where 𝛆ε=RU for a random variable R>0 and a vector U uniformly distributed on the unit sphere. The variables R and U need not be independent. Then F∼F(r−r0,n−r).

prp-glh-trinity.title: Wald, likelihood ratio and score
prp-glh-trinity.html: In the setting above, let u=SSH/SSE=qFH/(n−r). Then Wald=nu,−2log⁡Λ=nlog⁡(1+u),Score=nu1+u. Each is a strictly increasing function of FH, so the three tests, calibrated exactly, coincide with the F test. For every sample with SSH>0, Wald>−2log⁡Λ>Score. If each is compared with the upper α point c of χ2(q), the exact sizes are Pr{F(q,n−r)>n−rquc},uc=cn,ec/n−1,cn−c  (n>c) for the Wald, likelihood ratio and score tests respectively.

thm-glh-f-test.title: The F test of a reduced model
thm-glh-f-test.title_html: The F test of a reduced model
thm-glh-f-test.html:
Assume the normal linear model @eq-opt-normal-model and the setting of @def-glh-reduced-model, so that 0≤r0<r<n. Then:

  1. SSE0−SSE and SSE are independent, with SSE0−SSEσ2∼χ2(r−r0,γ),SSEσ2∼χ2(n−r);

  2. the statistic @eq-glh-F has the noncentral F distribution 𝛃F∼F(r−r0, n−r, γ),γ=‖(M−M0)Xβ‖2σ2;{#eq-glh-noncentrality}

  3. 𝛃𝛃γ=‖(I−M0)Xβ‖2/σ2=minc‖Xβ−X0c‖2/σ2, the squared distance from the mean vector to the reduced model space in units of σ2. In particular γ=0 iff H0 holds;

  4. under H0, F∼F(r−r0,n−r), the central F distribution, whatever the values of 𝛃β and σ2.

thm-glh-general-f.title: The F test of a testable hypothesis
thm-glh-general-f.title_html: The F test of a testable hypothesis
thm-glh-general-f.html:
Assume @eq-opt-normal-model with r<n, and let 𝛃H:Λ⊤β=d be testable with q=rank(Λ). Let G be any generalized inverse of X⊤X, 𝛃β^ any least squares estimate, W=Λ⊤GΛ and W− any generalized inverse of W. Put 𝛃𝛃SSH=(Λ⊤β^−d)⊤W−(Λ⊤β^−d),FH=SSH/qSSE/(n−r).{#eq-glh-general-F}

  1. SSH does not depend on the choices of 𝛃β^, G and W−.

  2. Let b0 be any solution of Λ⊤b0=d and S0={Xb:Λ⊤b=0}. Then S0 is a subspace of C(X) of dimension r−q, the set of mean vectors allowed by H is Xb0+S0, and SSH=minΛ⊤b=d‖y−Xb‖2−SSE=‖(M−PS0)(y−Xb0)‖2.

  3. FH∼F(q,n−r,γ) with 𝛃𝛃γ=(Λ⊤β−d)⊤W−(Λ⊤β−d)σ2,{#eq-glh-general-noncentrality}

    and γ=0 iff 𝛃Λ⊤β=d. In particular FH is the F statistic of @thm-glh-f-test for the data y−Xb0 and the reduced model space S0.

thm-glh-lrt.title: The F test is the likelihood ratio test
thm-glh-lrt.title_html: The F test is the likelihood ratio test
thm-glh-lrt.html:
Assume @eq-opt-normal-model with r<n, and let 𝛃H:Λ⊤β=d be testable with q=rank(Λ). Let SSEH=minΛ⊤b=d‖y−Xb‖2 and suppose SSE>0, which holds with probability one. Then:

  1. under H the likelihood is maximized at any minimizer 𝛃β^H of ‖y−Xb‖2 subject to Λ⊤b=d (for Λ of full column rank, the estimate of @prp-glh-restricted-ls; compare @thm-ss-restricted), with σ~H2=SSEH/n;

  2. the likelihood ratio is Λ=(SSESSEH)n/2=(1+qFHn−r)−n/2,{#eq-glh-lr}

    a strictly decreasing function of the statistic FH of @eq-glh-general-F;

  3. the likelihood ratio test of size α rejects exactly when FH>Fα(q,n−r).

The same holds for a reduced model E(Y)∈C(X0), with q=r−r0 and the statistic of @thm-glh-f-test.

thm-glh-power.title: Power of the F test
thm-glh-power.title_html: Power of the F test
thm-glh-power.html:
Assume @eq-opt-normal-model with r<n, and let 𝛃H:Λ⊤β=d be testable with q=rank(Λ) (or let H be a reduced model with q=r−r0). The probability that the level-α F test rejects is π(γ)=Pr{F(q,n−r,γ)>Fα(q,n−r)},{#eq-glh-power}

where γ is the noncentrality of @eq-glh-general-noncentrality, or of @eq-glh-noncentrality for a reduced model. Moreover:

  1. π depends on 𝛃(β,σ2) only through γ. It is continuous and strictly increasing, with π(0)=α and π(γ)→1 as γ→∞. In particular the test is unbiased: its power exceeds α at every alternative.

  2. σ2γ is the squared distance from the mean vector 𝛃Xβ to the set of mean vectors allowed by H: 𝛃𝛃σ2γ=minΛ⊤b=d‖Xβ−Xb‖2=minΛ⊤b=d∑i=1n(x(i)⊤β−x(i)⊤b)2.

  3. If further observations are added, with the same 𝛃β, σ2 and hypothesis, the noncentrality does not decrease. If the whole design is replicated k times, γ is multiplied by k.

thm-glh-t-test.title: The t test for an estimable function
thm-glh-t-test.title_html: The t test for an estimable function
thm-glh-t-test.html:
Assume @eq-opt-normal-model with r<n. Let 𝛌λ∈C(X⊤), 𝛌λ≠0, let d∈R, let G be a generalized inverse of X⊤X, and put 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌T=λ⊤β^−dsλ⊤Gλ,s2=SSEn−r.{#eq-glh-t}

  1. T∼t(n−r,δ) with 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌δ=(λ⊤β−d)/(σλ⊤Gλ).

  2. T2 equals the statistic FH of @eq-glh-general-F for 𝛌𝛃H:λ⊤β=d, and γ=δ2. The two-sided test that rejects when |T|>tn−r,α/2 is the F test of H, with the same p-value.

  3. The one-sided test that rejects when T>tn−r,α has size exactly α for the hypothesis 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β≤d: its rejection probability is at most α whenever 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β≤d, with equality when 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β=d. Its power increases strictly with 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β.

thm-glh-ump-invariant.title: The F test is uniformly most powerful invariant
thm-glh-ump-invariant.title_html: The F test is uniformly most powerful invariant
thm-glh-ump-invariant.html: Assume @eq-opt-normal-model and the setting of @def-glh-reduced-model. Let ϕ be an invariant test with Eϕ(Y)≤α at every point of H0. Then at every point 𝛃(β,σ2) of the full model, 𝛃Eβ,σ2ϕ(Y)≤Pr{F(q,n−r,γ)>Fα(q,n−r)}, with γ given by @eq-glh-noncentrality. The right side is the power of the F test, which is itself invariant and of size α.
